data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word ‘slōh’ which means ‘stream’, ‘broad valley’, or ‘plain’. In Irish, Sloan can be derived from ‘sloinn’, meaning ‘warlike’, or ‘red-haired’. The name Sloan carries the meaning “Stream or broad valley” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Sloan usually hope their child will grow to embody stream or broad valley and live with faith, good character and purpose.
